title: unicode-lexer-proxy-grapheme-boundary-safety-for-constrained-decoding
author: Asha Patel
description:
Motivation: Constrained decoding (CFG/regex backends) and the OpenAI compatibility layer were observing spurious mismatches when streaming responses contained multi-codepoint graphemes (emoji sequences, regional indicators, zero-width-joiner ligatures) or when deterministic Unicode normalization differed between constraint preprocessors and the runtime tokenizer. This caused structured-output validators and tool/function-calling to incorrectly reject partial or final outputs in production.

What I changed: Implemented a Unicode-aware \"lexer proxy\" that sits between the constraint backends (CFG, regex) and the tokenizer/streaming emitter. The proxy normalizes input sequences, exposes grapheme-boundary-aware token spans to the constraint engines, and adds a streaming-safe framing layer so we never emit a partial grapheme that could break a live constraint check. Key behaviors: NFKC normalization option (configurable), grapheme cluster segmentation using the Unicode Grapheme Cluster Boundary algorithm, mapping of grapheme spans to tokenizer token indices, and a small on-the-fly rewrite table for common emoji modifier/ZWJ sequences to maintain stable regex anchors. The proxy is pluggable so existing constraint backends can opt-in with minimal changes.

Why this is different from previous work: Prior PRs focused on tokenizer fallback heuristics and token-edge stitching. This PR resolves correctness at the grapheme/Unicode layer (pre-tokenization), preventing subtle mismatches when clients use regex/CFG constraints that assume character boundaries rather than BPE subtokens. It also improves streaming safety by ensuring constraint evaluation sees only whole grapheme units.

Files touched (high level): runtime/constraint/lexer_proxy.py, runtime/constraint/profiles/emoji_rewrites.json, runtime/constraint/tests/test_lexer_proxy.py, sdk/compat/openai_compat.ts (adjusted framing shim), docs/structured_output/unicode_compat.md, examples/structured-output/emoji-toolcall-example.json, infra/ci/constraint-integration.yml (added integration stage).

Commits (summary):
- Add Unicode-aware lexer proxy and grapheme segmentation utils
- Wire lexer proxy into CFG and regex backends behind feature flag
- Add rewrite table and normalization config; document behavior
- Add unit/integration tests covering emoji, ZWJ, regional indicators, and streaming truncation cases
- Fix openai_compat streaming shim to reject partial-grapheme frames
- CI: add constraint integration job and flake guard for tokenizer tests

Tests and CI: Local unit tests cover ~120 new cases for grapheme/token mapping and constraint satisfaction. Integration job runs a simulated streaming scenario with a tiny model (mock runtime) to ensure canary constraints don't regress. One unit test was flaky on first CI run (tokenizer fixture race); re-ran and marked as flake-guard with a short backoff — final CI status is green.

Usage notes and migration: This is enabled by default for new structured-output routes, but can be toggled via the \"unicode_lexer_proxy\" boolean in model constraint profiles for backwards compatibility. We added guidance in docs/structured_output/unicode_compat.md explaining interactions with regex anchors and recommended NFKC for user-supplied constraint grammars.

Rollout plan: Feature-flag gated across runtimes; Canary (10%) on hosted API for 48h, monitor structured-output rejection rate and streaming latency. No expected perf regression beyond a ~0.5–1ms per-request CPU cost for grapheme segmentation on short prompts; batching amortizes cost.

Related: ENG-3291 (structured-output stability), ENG-3410 (openai-compat framing issues).

review_thread: Miguel Torres: Nice, this addresses the root cause we saw in ENG-3291. Can you quantify worst-case CPU impact for long sequences?

Asha Patel: Added a microbenchmark in docs/structured_output/unicode_compat.md — worst-case single-request cost for 1k chars is ~6ms on a 4-core small instance; typical prompts are <200 chars so we expect ~0.5–1ms overhead. Batching and caching of segment maps reduces repeated work.
Leah Kim: I see potential interaction with existing token-prefix caching. Did you validate KV cache lookups still align when grapheme mapping changes token boundaries?

Asha Patel: Yes — we added deterministic mapping that is stable for tokenization changes if normalization mode is constant. There's a small note in the README about pinning normalization mode for long-lived caches.

Evan Ross: Tests look good. One nits: move the emoji rewrite table to profiles and load via existing profile loader. Also please add a short example to examples/structured-output showing a tool call with an emoji param.
Asha Patel: Done — moved the table and added example. Thanks.
Miguel Torres: Approved after the flake guard was added to CI. Verified canary metrics in staging show no spike in latency or rejection rate.
release_notes: Add Unicode-aware lexer proxy to improve structured-output constraint correctness and streaming safety for emoji, ZWJ sequences, regional indicators, and other multi-codepoint graphemes. Enabled by default for new routes; configurable via constraint profile.
notes: Backported approach considered for Dedicated/private deployments where customers can opt to keep legacy behavior by toggling the profile flag. Security review: no secrets involved; performance trade-offs documented.
